findings.finding: Imported rows_hash validation is a no-op and imported view metadata is assigned directly from decoded JSON without reconstructing its interval/cut/correction contract. Restore can accept changed rows_hash with no publications; malformed correction scope/counts can be admitted as retained evidence.
findings.repair: Normalize imported source rows to one explicit canonical order for hashing, validate view interval/cut/correction uniqueness/types/scope/bounds, and reject a mismatched retained hash. Add valid reordered-view and no-publication tamper tests.

findings.finding: Each query scans all event timestamps and rehashes the complete admission prefix before binary search. Each capture also reconstructs admissions, all leaf summaries and block-key hashes even when blocks are cached. The declared four-versus-twelve small source visits and 4096-versus32768 workload counters omit those physical source traversals.
findings.repair: Retain an immutable timestamp/index and precomputed immutable prefix proof in the capture; validate ownership/cursor without rewalking source rows. Count capture reconstruction, hashing, leaf creation, block construction and query/index work honestly. Keep build and query timing separate.

findings.finding: carry += pending.signed treats unknown signs as zero. Example events threshold1: unknown side size3 then buy size2. The second bar receives opening0 and exact CVD [0,2,0,2], although the true opening lies in [-3,3]. The literal independently traverses rows but duplicates the same wrong carry rule.
findings.repair: Carry an explicitly uncertain anchor after unknown signed mass; preserve available count/volume partitions while declining exact anchored CVD, and reset only on a named reset. Add unknown-first-block/known-next-block and reset-restores-zero cases in both implementations.

findings.finding: Read-only public properties do not protect reassignment/deletion of _domain/_definitions/_limits. Several public output dataclasses have no constructor validation. A replaced SharedBar can claim final=True via state='final', complete coverage, arbitrary publication or a forged summary and reach confirm_final_bars/opportunity_witness without retained publication proof.
findings.repair: Freeze admitted configuration slots and validate typed immutable public output records. Sanctioned downstream factories should require a factory-certified valid publication or reconstructible evidence, with replace/mutable nested inputs and forged finality/coverage assertions.

findings.finding: WindowCoverage accepts tuple elements that are mutable lists and does not apply timestamp/exact-int validation to each endpoint. WindowCoverage(..., observed_intervals=([0,10],), ...) can be mutated after request admission, changing coverage used by a supposedly immutable WindowRequest. Bool/float span endpoints can also pass comparisons.
findings.repair: Require immutable exact endpoint pairs, timestamp each endpoint, and strictly validate source/instrument identities. Re-read unchanged direct coverage consumers and add nested-mutation and bool/float interval cases.

findings.finding: The API materializes one activity definition per call and traverses every event again for each clock. The registered benchmark exercises only time queries, so it does not establish the promised shared one-pass count/volume/range materialization under multiple active clocks.
findings.location: multiresolution.py:publish_activity; protocol one-pass materialization; tests B26
findings.repair: Provide a bounded multi-definition whole-event dispatch or explicitly retain/count the per-clock work without claiming one shared pass. Add matched mixed-clock outputs and source/composition counters in the single registered finite workload; do not add repetitions or threshold searches.

findings.finding: Activity publication has no per-definition observation-cut/prefix regression check, unlike publish_window. An old capture can be published after a corrected/current capture at a later published_at and then become the newest value for an unchanged activity bar_id. Activity revision is always0, so version sequencing relies solely on insertion order.
findings.repair: Enforce monotone captured evidence for repeated activity materializations and retain explicit revision/publication order, while preserving saved historical captures as immutable audit evidence. Test old-capture publication after a correction and same-cut later admissions.

findings.finding: prefix_id hashes all admissions through cursor including entries whose known_at is after the captured cut. Adding/deleting an unavailable future suffix therefore changes a newly captured old-cut prefix ID and output version despite identical eligible events/corrections. B16 tests only an already stored publication, so it misses the stronger exact old-cut prefix invariant.
findings.repair: Separate admission cursor provenance from the causal eligible input identity or explicitly derive a cut-filtered prefix hash. Test reconstructing the same old cut after future additions/deletions and after same-cut later admission, retaining the intended distinction.

findings.finding: Activity end uses summary.last_at + 1 without timestamp validation on SharedBar. An otherwise valid Trade at maximum int64 time creates an out-of-domain endpoint. Public SharedBar also does not enforce interval nonemptiness, min-known/publication order, or valid state/revision types.
findings.repair: Validate computed endpoints and all publication scalar invariants before mutating retained state; reject an unrepresentable exclusive endpoint atomically. Include max-clock and malformed-publication cases.

findings.finding: The confirmation helper accepts any nonempty tuple of available complete bars, including duplicates, mixed definitions/instruments and arbitrary order. The B25 test passes one [0,4] aggregate under a descriptive 'two-right-final' name and therefore only proves a generic publication delay, not the frozen two-right-bar confirmation case.
findings.repair: Keep the generic helper honestly named/scoped or bind a declared confirmation rule to distinct ordered compatible bars. Exercise actual two-right-final evidence for the frozen thin fixture without claiming a hidden source predictor.

findings.finding: An explicit body_envelope is only checked against wick extrema, so a coarse bar with open100/close110 can claim body_envelope=(105,106). The merged result then purports to preserve a constituent body envelope that omits the supplied bar's endpoint bodies. Signed endpoint also reports buy-sell when unknown volume is positive without retaining endpoint bounds in CoarseAggregate.
findings.repair: Require an explicit constituent envelope to include the aggregate endpoints where those are known, and preserve signed support/unknown mass or expose bounds rather than an unqualified true endpoint when signs are incomplete. Add malformed envelope and unknown-side coarse cases.

findings.finding: Auxiliary public paths have weaker validation than shared trade admission: allocations do not revalidate original Trade clock/history/price contract, part_index and known_at equality can accept bool aliases, and quote bounds have no declared cardinality ceiling. These paths can undermine the stated exact immutable finite input contract even though ordinary Trade admission rejects allocations.
findings.repair: Apply exact typed/scalar checks and finite ceilings consistently to these auxiliary records/factories, retaining the distinction from independent trades. Add malformed bool/index/clock and over-bound auxiliary fixtures.

findings.finding: The activity parity helper compares forming summary only, omitting forming carry/epoch/state/overshoot and all per-bar interval/publication/correction/block lineage. There are no max-clock/max-publication/reset overflow atomic tests, activity checkpoint tamper/suffix tests, imported hash tamper tests or exact signed-order boundary permutations beyond simple examples.
findings.repair: Compare complete supported output/lineage fields and cover each declared limit/refusal path, valid activity restarts, reset placement, known/unknown carry and imported source evidence within the same registered suite.

findings.finding: Merging summaries repeatedly concatenates full event_ids/content_versions tuples and forms set intersections. Time queries still scan every block; activity pending merges can become quadratic in source identity copying for high thresholds. The workload reports compositions but not copied identity/source metadata volume, so it should not imply sublinear total work solely from summary count.
findings.repair: Use bounded indexed/range evidence or report this retained metadata work explicitly. The one toy timing may still pass without a speedup, but the comparison should distinguish arithmetic sharing from lineage copying and full construction costs.

findings.finding: Forming missing and final missing witnesses reuse the same bar/target/end identity with distinct versions. The intentional immutable opportunity conflict gate therefore raises before the intended eligible-count assertion.
findings.repair: Use distinct declared target definitions for the two separate denominator exclusion examples, and separately assert version substitution conflict for one opportunity. Keep the fixed expected eligible1/success0.

findings.finding: Even after filtering prefix_id to eligible inputs (I08), semantic version_id includes the admission cursor. An unavailable future admission suffix therefore still changes a reconstructed old-cut semantic version.
findings.repair: Retain cursor as audit/replay evidence while computing semantic version from eligible prefix identity and publication semantics. Compare freshly reconstructed identical old cuts with and without future additions and future corrections; retain the distinct same-cut later-admission behavior.

findings.finding: Legacy BarEngine and ActivityBars configuration and public collections remain assignable/mutable.
findings.repair: Freeze configuration and expose immutable views of retained publications/state while preserving BarEngine.ledger.correct access and narrow legacy callers.

findings.finding: Legacy BarEngine restore trusts plausible serialized price/volume outputs without publication input/coverage/watermark/prefix reconstruction.
findings.repair: Retain each admitted request and its actual ledger prefix, verify it is retained in the final ledger history and reconstruct every publication including prior same-cut cursors; enforce bounded publication retention.

findings.finding: Legacy ActivityBars restore does not reconstruct first threshold crossing and interleaved same-known-time resets; output close_reason and threshold flags can be forged.
findings.repair: Retain an ordered add/boundary operation journal and replay it; compare every completed/forming/output frontier field and exact canonical representation.

findings.finding: Legacy activity admission repeatedly sums all pending event quantities, creating quadratic work for high thresholds.
findings.repair: Use an exact pending-volume counter and reconstruct it through the retained operation journal; retain the old literal path as the bounded baseline, with no unsupported universal speedup claim.

findings.finding: Visit state differs from frozen F10-02: production and reference emit reclaim; expected state is reclaimed. Use explicit event-to-state conversion in both independent implementations.

_refresh_hot calls active_set after every commit; _views enumerates and decodes every historical birth, including archived objects. active/relation capacity queries scan full records each commit; restore repeats full _views for each suffix batch. Replace with bounded current projections and targeted hot updates; separately count all SQL/index/decode work.

events_asof, visits_asof and _visit_heads materialize unbounded history. Observation admission scans every old visit merely to find open visit/next ordinal. relations_asof materializes global relations before object filtering. Add bounded pagination and object-local current visit/relation indexes; preserve named fixture API behavior within bounds.

TTL archive excludes hot IDs but capacity counts still treat expired-by-TTL births as active forever. Relation capacity retains all non-tombstoned inactive history. Use frozen lifetime policy for hot capacity, retain durable history, and prevent visits/fallback on TTL-expired or invalid-instrument objects.

Ancestry RelationVersion changes ancestry table only; it adds no reverse dependencies or support gating. Parent invalidation through relation-only edges does not reach child. Include current relation ancestry in support/dirty propagation; tombstone must update affected projection without altering historical cuts.

Mapping evidence may be omitted from evidence_versions and dependencies; it is not required to be latest, so mapping correction may never gate mapped object. Anchor evidence instrument is not checked; cross-instrument parent mapping checks only mapping existence, not exact parent source. Validate full mapping/source/anchor instrument closure and include mapping source dependencies.

PublicationClock accepts completion before decision_cut. Object/anchor/observation dependencies are checked against final publication rather than frozen input cut; past declared known_at can conceal later effective batch publication. Define staged earlier-member exception explicitly, check prior-row effective known time and required inputs against decision/input clocks; reject future event facts where inappropriate.

Observation admission uses any old observed evidence version without checking latest support, evidence_state, instrument validity or TTL. Unknown-order ENTER/CONTACT can open a visit, and unknown distinct timestamp ordering is accepted without clear source evidence policy. Validate event support and preserve unknown chronology explicitly.

fallback(previous_valid) calls _support against latest entire database for historical cut, causing future correction leakage. It ignores TTL, evidence_state and terminal expired/superseded birth restrictions and can return current version as prior fallback. Use as-of support and explicit valid prior policy/provenance.

Checkpoint/audit validate saved payloads but omit births, dependencies, ancestry, record metadata known/sequence/identity/ordinal, state known/sequence metadata, extra injected rows and control metadata. Tampering can pass and change queries or next updates. Journal must be authority: fully verify/rebuild all derived indexes with measured integrity work and exact-prefix binding.

lineage_payload uses separate read transactions, so concurrent commit can mix cursors. Instrument filter affects objects only; observations/visits/relations/targets/actions remain global. candidate_cut may be future or mismatched instrument/cursor. Build one snapshot at one cursor, validate cut compatibility and complete instrument-specific closure; distinguish requested cut from actual known publication.

Canonical source origins are only required to be a subset of closure and remain caller ordered. Empty/subset/reordered origins can produce multiple birth identities for same formation. Normalize unordered origin IDs and enforce the intended complete origin closure while preserving declared anchor order; account for parent source closure in split/merge fixtures.

RegistryDefinition permits terminal initial states and arbitrary tuple ordering/duplicate generator IDs with different versions; semantic version is separate hash while id can remain same. Clarify frozen definition identity and reject impossible birth lifecycle configurations.

Production implicit parent_versions ancestry is not exposed by relations_asof or candidate relation closure. Freeze only captures relations incident to current latest versions, omitting parent/anchor/evidence/transitive original versions. Preserve full exact candidate lineage closure, including archived intermediate ancestors, without conflating display and ancestry.

Control APIs return mutable nested dict/list values despite immutable public-record contract. Values are detached from durable storage but public immutability is not enforced. Return deeply immutable mappings/tuples or canonical bytes consistently.

Reference ignores reset_on_geometry_change configuration; it shares missing mapping/relation support behavior. assert_parity compares objects, state, visits, relations, cuts and targets but never action groups or all version membership. Add independent config-aware fold and full closure comparisons.

Coverage gaps against frozen literals: F10-03 lacks saved uninterrupted baseline; F10-04 lacks explicit post-rejection all-table absence; F10-21 uses preset labels but no immutable ratio/config provenance; F10-24/25 omit explicit uncertified mapping/replay assertions; F10-29 corrupt checkpoint fields without recomputed checksum, does not duplicate suffix B3 or assert zero prefix derivation; F10-31 lacks explicit two unfrozen equal-time cursor assertions. Other expected boolean fields are implicit/hardcoded rather than mapped exact assertions. Expand existing 34 methods with every frozen expected field and complete failure/no-mutation checks.

F10-28 saves pre-update telemetry under incremental_telemetry_before_restore, so no after/delta adjacency/read costs retained. query_parity includes full reference construction and all queries, not isolated indexed query time; restore telemetry contaminated by assert_parity; object_evaluations excludes admission/support recursion and full hot scans. Capture before/after deltas, raw exact operation counts, isolated query/restore and named retained IO/decode costs; no speedup claim.

Source correction batch dirty propagation can create more derived payload than allowed; atomic rejection is correct but no resumable bounded dirty closure exists. Keep explicit capacity_unavailable gate and document that finite limits bound total accepted closure rather than claiming arbitrary targeted scaling.

verify.py labels legacy objects group with F10.LINEAGE even though it only loads tests.test_objects; new object-lineage group is correct. Parent should remove lineage certification from legacy-only owner mapping or label declaration versus executed coverage explicitly.

Numerical setting key is libraries while frozen base evidence uses library_versions. Set-like fit membership, labels and fold routes/population are not canonically ordered. Equivalent declarations can create different IDs.
findings.repair: Use frozen numerical key and normalize genuinely set-like tuples while retaining actual model input ordering. Add equality assertions for reordered configuration/membership/dependency declarations.

findings.finding: Some enum checks accept malformed hashable values or leak TypeError for unhashable inputs; CommitRef/ClosureManifest/VerifiedCommit have no type checks, limits argument is unchecked, and the serializer admits a foreign dataclass solely by matching its class name. Fold population uses a hardcoded 4096 rather than an admitted lower configured bound.
findings.repair: Validate exact scalar/record types at public boundaries, constrain serializer by exact registered class, and enforce configured population/read cardinality bounds before graph/content processing.

findings.finding: An audit-purpose label read can be placed in a prediction read manifest. Prediction validation checks row/cut but does not forbid audit or fit_label purposes. A label can also be hidden behind a provenance edge in a fold-independent feature.
findings.repair: Enforce purpose-specific direct read edges and deny labels through inference/feature value ancestry; require prediction reads to be sanctioned inference purposes and retain audit-only manifests outside inference roots. Add negative label/audit laundering assertions.

findings.finding: Prediction usability checks only its own row validity. A source with valid_until=120 can feed a prediction row declaring valid_until=140; the output remains usable at129. The current test only shortens the output manually and misses inheritance.
findings.repair: Derive inherited expiry from every actual-read dependency and reject or tighten a later output validity endpoint. Exercise source-derived expiry at119/120 and same-cut derived completion without double charge.

findings.finding: Training labels lack retained original target start/end evidence and their row clocks are not reconciled with population label_known_at/dependency_end. A caller can attach the requested target reference to an unrelated label row. Training reads can use a decision_cut later than the sample's original decision.
findings.repair: Retain label target definition/endpoints on the label node, compare exact sample/target endpoints and maturity, and enforce each training feature's original sample decision cut. Add forged target, late feature and future label assertions.

findings.finding: Bindings in one session can mix row IDs, cuts, assembly times, purposes and fold routes. Request fold nodes need not belong to the read manifest's dependency closure. Actual reads need only appear somewhere in ancestry rather than their declared direct column slot.
findings.repair: Pin coherent immutable session configuration, enforce direct slot/node/column/purpose bindings and retained fold dependencies, preserve heterogeneous explicitly declared per-column schema/units, and add nested/configuration mutation assertions.

findings.finding: Cross-fold routes are keyed by descriptive logical_key rather than exact producer semantic ID. The gate accepts an arbitrary caller-constructed ClosureManifest/VerifiedCommit without verifying its fit evidence. It also allows an absent target request and does not reconcile request endpoints/decision with the retained population.
findings.repair: Bind routes to exact producer IDs and retained fold contracts, require validated closure evidence at the public gate, and enforce exact sample/group/target/original clocks. Add missing population, same-date, future ancestor and route-substitution checks on the real candidate.

findings.finding: All reads/labels declared in FitEvidence are checked, but extra fit-label dependencies or additional actual-read manifests can be present and not reconciled as part of actual training use. Empty training membership is accepted when the retained fold is empty. Prediction row evidence may incorrectly claim received availability.
findings.repair: Require exact training-label/read evidence correspondence, nonempty fitted training rows for this finite model family, and explicit derived prediction lineage. Preserve all read provenance including zero-effect/diagnostic paths.

findings.finding: The served session may belong to another store/commit or supply audit-purpose values, while the OOF gate checks only the model commit. Payload attestation validates a root dataclass's bytes but not actual nested base/calibrator/scaler state against the semantic fitted ancestors and target/column configuration. New model methods are not tested.
findings.repair: Require the session's exact admitted commit/configuration, revalidate every actual read against that closure, reconcile actual model and nested transform/calibrator state and input order, and exercise BinaryModel, FrequencyModel and CalibratedBinary adapters with finite supplied state before their arithmetic.

findings.finding: Concurrent writers can independently pass byte/count limits and together exceed them. Same-key conflicting racing writers raise the publication primitive's IntegrityError rather than the declared commit conflict error. A mutable payload mapping can change between validation and staging.
findings.repair: Snapshot immutable proposed payloads and serialize finite store mutation with a local file lock; recheck configuration/accounting/idempotence under that lock and preserve one-pointer success semantics.

findings.finding: Semantic manifests are stored in the payload blob directory and charged against max_store_blob_bytes rather than reported separately. Orphan manifest bytes, failed-attempt audit bytes and the mutation-lock accounting are not separated. Reopen does not enforce aggregate retained byte/count ceilings.
findings.repair: Separate bounded manifest storage and accounting from unique content payloads, include retained orphan/staging/audit costs in reporting, and validate aggregate configured ceilings without eviction. Update exact small store-bound assertions accordingly.

findings.finding: A commit key is unbounded; a pointer may be larger than max_manifest_bytes even if the manifest fits, making successful publication unreadable. Restore checks canonical JSON but not a byte-for-byte canonical typed re-encoding after constructors normalize fields, and manifest_ref.kind is not enforced.
findings.repair: Bound pointer/key envelopes before publication, enforce manifest kind and canonical typed re-encoding on restore, and retain proper corruption/absence distinctions.

findings.finding: Rebuild accepts unvalidated proposed node tuples and checks missing edges but not full graph/role/fit validity or cycles. It trusts an arbitrary previous closure, and does not ensure unchanged consumers bind the actual revised dependency identities before declaring rebuilt/reused sets.
findings.repair: Require or derive validated old/proposed closures with exact roots, configured bounds and bytes, then compute reverse adjacency and assert reusable IDs/causal first-change paths. Add undeclared dependency/code/source changes and malformed proposed graph assertions.

findings.finding: The incremental arithmetic test supplies the frozen expected affected set directly to candidate evaluation instead of using the candidate invalidation plan. The semantic metric graph uses placeholder checkpoint states unrelated to the arithmetic values, so same full/incremental semantic manifest parity is not demonstrated.
findings.repair: Build semantic specs from the independently frozen toy recipes and actual candidate outputs, derive affected keys from plan_rebuild, execute affected-only arithmetic, and compare full/incremental exact values and semantic manifests. Report build/restore validation and arithmetic work separately in ENGINEERING_METRICS.

findings.finding: Failed audit records accept arbitrary trial/attempt strings and can reference unstored partial bytes; there is no reconciliation to TrialRegistry. The test has only two string audits plus one commit and does not actually establish one renamed scientific trial, three attempts or reservation charging/restart history.
findings.repair: Reconcile failed/interrupted evidence to a real temporary TrialRegistry state and retained partial refs; test the registered three synthetic attempts, scientific-name aliasing, unknown usage charge and successful commit reference without changing generic TrialRegistry semantics.

findings.finding: The future-fit variant removes prediction and then only validates a fit completing at101. That is a valid standalone completed fit, so the asserted ContractError has no reason to occur. Candidate tests cover one model, while three-ancestor golden checks run only the literal helper.
findings.repair: Exercise future completion at the actual OOF request gate and construct a valid retained scaler/model/calibrator closure with individual same-date/sample/future/missing-population corruptions.

findings.finding: Role rejection calls private _admit on an incomplete synthetic ClosureManifest; the golden downstream OOF admissible case is not tested through a real later fold. The seven-node DAG fixture labels every node checkpoint and cycle rejection is only literal-reference-side.
findings.repair: Use validated real role closures and sanctioned reads for label/OOF/final admission, preserve the exact seven-node graph shape as an explicit shape-only subcase, and add candidate stage/missing/cycle/extra closure assertions with honest role evidence.

findings.finding: Several golden consequences are asserted indirectly or with substitute values: training normalization is local test arithmetic only; same-value source invalidation changes checkpoint state; reconstruction omits typed fitted components; numerical decision only uses reference; keepalive/no invented pairing are not exercised as admission constraints.
findings.repair: Connect these assertions to the corresponding retained candidate row/source/fit/target and numerical APIs, derive expected values solely from frozen literals/reference, and explicitly identify provenance-only EXT-031 scope without claiming acquisition or flow reconstruction.

findings.finding: Coverage is missing for deep mutable audit state, required-to-optional mutation, source-derived expiry, corrupted checkpoint content, commit root/pointer corruption, concurrent bound enforcement, orphan byte accounting and the exact over-limit/no-partial paths. The initial broad ValueError assertion can hide an incorrect error class.
findings.repair: Add these bounded negative assertions with exact contract error classes and unchanged previous-commit checks; keep actual process-death checks restricted to supervised future execution.

findings.finding: Reference graph/arithmetic/fold gates are independent but actual-read and retained target/stage closure validation are not represented; prediction_available is unused. The reference alone cannot substantiate all claimed three-stage comparisons.
findings.repair: Add bounded primitive read/role/target/fit validation and invoke it against frozen fixtures beside candidate outcomes; preserve independence from candidate constructors and manifest helpers.

findings.finding: Every by_id access repeatedly hashes full semantic records, including nested fit/read evidence, and closure validation repeatedly constructs those mappings. This can inflate finite build/restore work unnecessarily, particularly at registered node limits.
findings.repair: Cache the already-computed immutable ID-to-node index inside validated closure construction and retain explicit work accounting rather than calling validation free.

findings.finding: Configuration and source mapping are guarded, but the public object has a mutable __dict__ and _read mapping; direct nested mutation can forge or erase actual reads. The older compatibility audit also silently lists unused optional fields without an explicit omission reason.
findings.repair: Use slots and immutable recorded-read replacement, add explicit permitted optional omission handling while retaining existing required-by-default callers and manifest compatibility, and test mutation/repeated-read behavior.

findings.finding: Ordinary computed source/measurement/feature nodes are not subject to actual-read or inherited causal-clock validation. A future source row known at 200 can be a value/provenance dependency of a feature row whose caller-declared input_known_at is 100. Neither validate_closure nor _admit traverses those external row clocks for the feature; the feature may be read at cut 100. This does not require a label or fitted ancestor, so repairing R03 label laundering and R04 prediction expiry alone does not close it.
findings.repair: Require explicit retained row-level read/derivation evidence for computed measurement/feature nodes and reconcile every used external row against the original decision cut, inherited validity, actual completion and same-cut assembly. Externally supplied rows must remain explicitly external sources rather than unverified computed rows. Add a future-source -> ordinary-feature -> sanctioned input rejection and a legitimate same-cut derived positive case.

findings.finding: validate_oof_producer checks that the requested sample exists in the population and has the declared date, but never that it belongs to the request fold evaluation_ids. A purged sample outside the evaluation block, excluded from every producer training set, can pass as an OOF sample by retaining the true group and a compatible earlier fit. Exact population/target/time checks proposed in R07 should explicitly include evaluation membership and evaluation boundaries.
findings.repair: Require the requested row to be an actual evaluation member of the authoritative request fold, with its retained decision inside that fold interval; preserve independently declared cross-fold producer routes. Include a purged/outside-evaluation row negative case at the real OOF gate.

findings.finding: The committed adapter performs float(_json(...)) without the existing finite scalar validator and checks only math.isfinite(result). Canonical JSON strings such as "Infinity" and booleans become floats; an infinite input to BinaryModel may yield sigmoid(infinity)=1 and pass the final finite check. Supplied FrequencyModel probabilities/cell counts/prior and BinaryModel scales are not domain-validated either, so finite out-of-range probabilities or zero-division can escape the intended typed admission. Matching immutable bytes is insufficient numerical validation.
findings.repair: Before arithmetic, accept only the registered finite scalar representation, reject strings/bools/nonfinite values, validate positive scales and finite coefficients/intercepts, coherent frequency counts/prior/cuts and calibration floor, and validate output with the probability contract. Preserve existing arithmetic for valid supplied state. Add negative adapter cases without fitting a model.

findings.finding: serve_bound_model unconditionally calls validate_oof_producer for every binding, including final-purpose requests. ReadRequest permits final requests without date_group/fold_node_id, so a legitimate final inference request necessarily fails the OOF fold check; a valid final model with prior training exposure also fails even when final inference target/time checks should govern. This is a distinct positive-path integration failure, not only the cross-session bypass in R09.
findings.repair: Dispatch explicitly by coherent session purpose: OOF uses authoritative evaluation exclusion and routes; final uses its own admitted fitted-state completion, target, row, horizon and input checks. Reject audit/fit-label purposes for serving. Add positive final and OOF committed adapter cases for supported model classes, plus wrong target/clock negatives.

findings.finding: Finite row/column/read/configuration size admission happens after semantic ID construction. validate_closure hashes every full node at line 484 before row/column bounds; arbitrary execution configuration bytes, row value bytes, namespace/slot strings or oversized nested read evidence can cause large recursive encoding before max_manifest_bytes is checked in commit. The configured payload bound only checks referenced blob sizes and does not bound these embedded semantic fields before hashing. ReadSession also has no standalone binding cardinality bound.
findings.repair: Add lightweight exact type/count/embedded-byte-size validation before recursive canonicalization or hashing, and enforce a bounded session declaration/manifest size before per-binding resolution. Retain the registered ceilings rather than silently truncating. Add bounded over-limit sentinels that prove rejection occurs before encoding/IO.

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: EligibilityIndex.snapshot expects (FieldKey, policy.id), but by_name supplies OperationPolicy. Both entry and protection paths need IDs; T13/T14/T20/T24 otherwise fail.
findings.title: quality callback policy key

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: Semantic parity omits instrument/definition and control payload identities. recorded_action is transport in market/publication; changed buy/sell can classify transport_only. Include action, served vector, source identity and relevant control semantics in driver/reference, preserving timing separation and explicit numeric difference diagnostics.
findings.title: semantic observation completeness

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: F05/publication/order wrappers map ordinal to known/completed times without rejecting actual_capture. Require synthetic/model-only inputs and explicit logical clock scope; raw retained actual records are not wrapper-certified UTC evidence.
findings.title: logical clock wrapper gate

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: last_economic omits initial_events; first older replay ACK can bypass wrapper stale gate. Same economic-known/version with contradictory payload is accepted; rejected stale ACK IDs are not retained for immutable-ID conflict checks. Seed initial boundary, retain all identities, reject contradictory same versions.
findings.title: order restart and immutable version

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: Valid transaction body tagged snapshot can enter F05 because semantic_kind trade is not required. Gate it and add concrete T08 boundary assertion.
findings.title: F05 snapshot admission

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: F05 quantity silently switches to last instrument; publication version IDs alias across source/instrument/definition. Bind explicit immutable scope or typed identities; generic market toy scope also needs declared constraints.
findings.title: wrapper source scope

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: Repeated disconnect moves outage start; connected generation A-B-A and subscription reuse can pass; same-epoch boot marker accepted. Preserve first outage, track used epochs, retain opening and closing gap evidence.
findings.title: control epochs and outage evidence

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: Journal inspection/append call semantic control validation before raw commit, so structurally valid generation/sequence faults are rejected without raw retention or labelled archive corruption. Separate structural journal checks from replay semantic admission.
findings.title: raw retention before control admission

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: Existing empty archive silently initialized; quarantine releases source lock before copy and destination existence check races; hex tail evidence can exceed bound. Exclusive creation, immutable original/held lock or verified pin, and bounded binary evidence required.
findings.title: archive creation and quarantine

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: Caller can forge durable_local_journal on CommittedArrival; actual dispatch gate trusts string. Exact retry checks record SHA but not archived prefix proof. Require internal proof or explicit narrower trust contract plus retry proof validation.
findings.title: commit proof trust boundary

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: Replay callback/trace/definition/policy fields are mutable; quality entry/protection lists remain mutable after hash; journal path mutable. Freeze configuration and captured collections.
findings.title: immutable configuration

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: Unhashable enum/name inputs, surrogate Unicode and wrong body containers can raise TypeError/UnicodeError/AttributeError. Normalize bounded schema rejection before dispatch; add T34 cases.
findings.title: schema error normalization

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: Callback counter increments only on successful commit despite failed calls executed. Track attempted versus committed work; disclose full history serialization/rebuild scope instead of suggesting callbacks measure all work.
findings.title: attempted work metrics

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: delay_one sorts and rewrites trace IDs before validating original full trace, silently repairing invalid order/identity. Validate original first. T22 uses 3 source deliveries plus explicit decision at global ordinal 3; third source global ordinal 4 while conceptual eligible source list is [1,2,3]. Golden unchanged; selected original ordinal 2 and first cut25 retained.
findings.title: counterfactual original validation

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: latency_summary trusts arbitrary dict qualified flags; no bound, dedup or known method enforcement. Validate retained clock/provenance qualification, source identity, bounded unique sample identities and conflicts; actual_live_evidence remains false.
findings.title: telemetry evidence qualification

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: Absent available_operations defaults to requested operation and grants capability. Require explicit synthetic operation evidence and update fixture input; disclose joint span constant or bind immutable policy.
findings.title: quality capability evidence

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: Completion start clock not tied to job submission; duplicate business signature omits changed start clock. Publication timer duplicates timer ID; market timer ignores conflicting due info. Bind submission clocks and immutable completion/timer signatures.
findings.title: publication completion and timers

findings.finding_and_proposed_repair: Several tests assert golden constants for no effects, recovery dispatch and unsupported claims. Add observable fail-on-live-call guards, write/partial-write poisoning and no decode, malformed callback rollback, mutable config rejection, actual wrapper gate, F05 snapshot and core action parity assertions within registered cases. Existing fsync/decode/torn recovery and restart assertions are meaningful.
findings.title: assertion gaps

findings.detail: The worker uses per-process RLIMIT_CPU and process.wait(timeout=240), while F11/F12 fork real child workers. Multiple processes can exceed the shared 180-second physical-attempt reservation without any individual process exceeding its CPU limit.
findings.finding: Aggregate attempt CPU is not enforced
findings.repair: Poll aggregate live group CPU plus reaped child CPU, avoiding double counting, and terminate at the frozen aggregate soft limit; preserve the hard per-process and wall limits and retain observed resource charges.

findings.detail: A parsed result can be non-None but omit artifact/code_snapshot or reference missing/corrupt bytes. Exception handling preserves that result in durable interrupted completion. finalize indexes and copies those fields before finishing any family, and recovery repeats the same failing operation.
findings.finding: Malformed result can permanently strand reserved attempts
findings.repair: Validate result schema and referenced artifacts before accepting it as a verification result; preserve malformed raw output separately, then terminalize interrupted members with available evidence and correct charges. Artifact-copy failure must remain explicitly recoverable without a worker rerun.

findings.detail: Recovery identifies inherited worker argv in fork descendants but calls killpg(child PID), although descendants remain in the original leader process group. After leader death this misses the executable group and live_groups retains the gate indefinitely.
findings.finding: Leader death leaves live fork descendants unrecoverable
findings.repair: Resolve and validate actual process-group identity from surviving exact-command descendants and retained launch identity before group termination. Retain process start identity so PID reuse cannot be confused with the original worker.

findings.detail: The new supervisor gates on unresolved lifecycle files also used by the older F05-F08 supervisor, but --recover requires acknowledgement worker_source to equal the new script. An older unresolved run therefore receives a recovery instruction the new command cannot fulfill.
findings.finding: Shared lifecycle directory has incompatible recovery routing
findings.repair: Record and validate supervisor identity per lifecycle and dispatch or print the exact owning recovery command for foreign runs. Never launch another worker to recover.

findings.detail: Metrics collection accepts any dictionary including empty, validates JSON finiteness only, and is triggered by any passed test in a module. Recorder relays these values without checking mandatory fields or that the performance/parity assertion ran successfully.
findings.finding: Metrics presence is weaker than frozen performance evidence requirements
findings.repair: Specify a finite schema for each family, bind it to the exact successful performance assertion identity, and validate required timing/memory/counter/parity fields and bounds before marking success or attaching evidence.

findings.detail: Review preflight checks existing disposition values and supplied identity lists; empty dispositions or omitted reviewer reports pass those conditions. It does not compare disposition keys with the union of required collected finding IDs.
findings.finding: Preflight does not prove all collected findings received a disposition
findings.repair: Require the batch review to enumerate the intended implementation and orchestration reviews, resolve every finding ID exactly once, reject omitted/extra dispositions, and retain those exact reviewed sources and repair reports.

findings.detail: Mapping metadata hashes the normalizer but the code snapshot excludes tools and preflight retains supervisor and recorder only. A later mapping cannot be reproduced from retained script bytes unless separately added to the review input list.
findings.finding: Mapping script provenance is not retained with execution
findings.repair: Retain the normalizer bytes and its exact source inputs in preflight and bind mapping input hashes to those artifacts and frozen registration source bytes.

scope: Finite shared engineering cases; no phase/source/native/economic closure inferred
